_readme: Little Thing of Nowa, ep.01 — why the device has no touchscreen. SECOND PASS,
re-planned against the rules that did not exist when the first cut was made:
the layout library, the full-frame/panel balance cap, the static-hold limit and
the cutaway floor. The first pass was 5 of 9 cards as callout:panel.
The argument: what it actually has (a screen, a scroller, a button) → the TikTok
kid pinch-zooming a paper album → they will learn touch anyway, and voice too →
so the physical interactions are the ones being lost → the BlackBerry scroller →
five senses, and touch only uses one → a button gives many kinds of feedback →
we could have made a glass slab, and it would have been boring.
Balance: every card is a different presentation, full-frame is held under the 25%
cap, and nothing sits still for more than 8s without something landing on a word.
Sourced stills (3), all credited on screen from media/sources.json:
b05b  an open paper album, CC BY 4.0 — the object in the anecdote
b13   a BlackBerry 7290, the correct trackwheel generation, found through
Google Images; plus a CC BY 2.0 trackball macro beside it
The 7290 replaced a public-domain Bold 9700, which was the wrong generation
(trackpad, not a wheel) and forced a hedged caption. The licensed libraries
have nothing of the trackwheel era at usable resolution — checked Openverse
and Commons for 8700 / 7290 / 6230 before going wider.

beats.intent: hook — series brand and the question
'a physical screen, not a touchscreen' — the screen macro beside his demo
the two controls, literally — the wheel on the top edge, then the buttons
no-text: ring the wheel while he names it
a breath before the anecdote — glide over finished units
the anecdote — no footage exists, so type carries it, landing in two beats

card.text: A kid tried to pinch-zoom / a paper photo album

beats.intent: the object itself, landing on the words — an inset so he stays on screen for the punchline

card.caption: A paper album. No pinch, no zoom.

beats.intent: the dad's face — an aside, so a sticker
picture beat: they learn touch anyway. A photograph, full-bleed, nothing on it.
picture beat: and voice is next
the thesis line, at poster scale

card.text: The physical ones / are being lost

beats.intent: 'for example, the scroller' — the wheel in context
where the scroller came from — a public-domain photograph, credited

card.title: The first BlackBerry / he ever owned
card.caption: Controls you could work without looking.

beats.intent: the controls he loved, each lighting as he reaches it — no footage of a BlackBerry exists, and the argument is the sequence

items.what: A wheel on the side edge
A flat pad. Then just glass.

beats.intent: five senses — the number is the whole point

card.label: senses
card.sub: The more of them a thing touches, the more fun it is

beats.intent: no-text: of five senses, touch lights one
the flat glass he is describing
picture beat: a finger on glass, on the words that describe it
the contrast, as two plates, arriving one at a time

left.head: A SCREEN
items: Eyes, then a finger on glass

beats.intent: the physical side — loose silicone buttons, then a finger on one
his own line, in a panel so the footage still reads

card.text: A big fan of physical buttons

beats.intent: picture beat: the glass slab he could have built
the road not taken, in his own words

card.title: A choice of how to interact

beats.intent: 'more variety of interaction' — the finished units
'the way toy should be' — close on the batch
picture beat: the way a toy should be — a handheld with buttons you can feel
sign-off over the goodbye and the tail
